blocks.content: USER sets which user account subsequent instructions, and the container's process at runtime, actually run as. Getting this right is one of the simplest, highest-impact security decisions in a Dockerfile.
USER appuser switches execution to a specific, usually non-privileged, user account for everything after it in the Dockerfile, and for the container's main process once it starts.

blocks.alt: Execution switches to a specific, named user

blocks.content:
RUN adduser --disabled-password appuser
USER appuser
CMD ["node", "index.js"]

blocks.content: 2. Without It, You Are root by Default
blocks.text: 2. Without It, You Are root by Default

blocks.content: If a Dockerfile never includes a USER instruction, the container runs as root by default, the same as any other Linux process that does not explicitly drop privileges.

blocks.alt: No USER instruction means root, silently

blocks.content: 3. Why This Actually Matters for Security
blocks.text: 3. Why This Actually Matters for Security

blocks.content: If an attacker manages to exploit a vulnerability inside a container running as root, they have root inside that container, a meaningfully worse starting position than if the process were already running as an unprivileged user. This is covered in full depth in the Docker Security module, USER is the single most direct control over it.

blocks.alt: Root inside a container is a worse starting point if compromised

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: USER switches the running process to a specific, ideally non-root, account, without it a container silently runs as root.
This is a real security control, not a formality, it directly limits the blast radius of anything that goes wrong inside the container.
